## The Project

**PAST-FORWARD** aims to develop and implement innovative climate adaptation strategies and a design support system for adaptive Historic Urban Landscape (HUL) planning while integrating geospatial analysis, participatory planning, and adaptive urban landscape design.

By leveraging living labs in the historic cities of Delft and Rotterdam (NL) and Xi’an and Guangzhou (CN), the project will test innovative approaches to resilience and future-oriented urban development.

**PAST-FORWARD** ensures that adaptation strategies are socially inclusive, technically robust, and policy-relevant through stakeholder-driven co-design.

**PAST-FORWARD** integrates work in China and the Netherlands to:

1.  Develop a portfolio of adaptive design strategies for socio-ecologically inclusive, climate-proof HULs;

2.  Create advanced open digital tools to inform, drive, and monitor these strategies, facilitating co-creative and participatory design processes;

3.  Validate and implement these strategies through pilot projects serving as living labs, balancing immediate actions with long-term perspectives;

4.  Provide regulatory recommendations to promote climate adaptation within governance frameworks.

## The Cities

::: pf-section-label
Where we work
:::

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(leaflet)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(sf)

cities <- data.frame(
  name = c("Delft", "Rotterdam", "Xi'an", "Guangzhou"),
  lat  = c(52.0116, 51.9244, 34.3416, 23.1291),
  lng  = c(4.3571,  4.4777,  108.9398, 113.2644),
  anchor = c("cities.qmd#delft", "cities.qmd#rotterdam",
             "cities.qmd#xian", "cities.qmd#guangzhou")
)

cities$popup <- paste0(
  "<strong>", cities$name, "</strong><br>",
  "<a href='", cities$anchor, "'>View living lab &rarr;</a>"
)

# highlight the Netherlands and China via Natural Earth country boundaries
countries <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")
highlight_countries <- countries[countries$iso_a3 %in% c("NLD", "CHN"), ]

leaflet(
  cities, width = "100%", height = "420px",
  options = leafletOptions(minZoom = 3, maxZoom = 14)
) |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron) |>
  addPolygons(
    data = highlight_countries,
    fillColor = "#E43D12",
    fillOpacity = 0.15,
    color = "#E43D12",
    weight = 1,
    opacity = 0.6
  ) |>
  addCircleMarkers(
    lng = ~lng, lat = ~lat,
    popup = ~popup,
    label = ~name,
    radius = 8,
    color = "#E43D12",
    fillColor = "#EBE9E1",
    fillOpacity = 0.9,
    weight = 2,
    clusterOptions = markerClusterOptions()
  ) |>
  fitBounds(min(cities$lng), min(cities$lat), max(cities$lng), max(cities$lat)) |>
  setMaxBounds(lng1 = -180, lat1 = -85, lng2 = 180, lat2 = 85)
```

## Work Packages

PAST-FORWARD is structured around four interconnected Work Packages (WPs), each addressing key research gaps in adapting Historic Urban Landscapes to climate change.

```{=html}
<div class="pf-wp-grid">

  <a class="pf-wp-card" href="work-packages.qmd#wp1">
    <p class="pf-wp-number">WP1</p>
    <p class="pf-wp-title">Framework Development &amp; Integration</p>
    <p class="pf-wp-lead">TU Delft &amp; SCUT</p>
    <p class="pf-wp-desc">A shared framework and methodology that merges climate resilience with heritage preservation across the Dutch and Chinese case studies.</p>
  </a>

  <a class="pf-wp-card" href="work-packages.qmd#wp2">
    <p class="pf-wp-number">WP2</p>
    <p class="pf-wp-title">Data-Driven Adaptation Planning</p>
    <p class="pf-wp-lead">TU Delft &amp; SCUT</p>
    <p class="pf-wp-desc">A digital atlas, GIS-based toolkit, and web-based Decision Support System to inform and monitor adaptation planning.</p>
  </a>

  <a class="pf-wp-card" href="work-packages.qmd#wp3">
    <p class="pf-wp-number">WP3</p>
    <p class="pf-wp-title">Adaptive Design Principles</p>
    <p class="pf-wp-lead">XAUAT &amp; TU Delft</p>
    <p class="pf-wp-desc">Context-specific, heritage-sensitive design principles and strategies, validated through pilot projects in the living labs.</p>
  </a>

  <a class="pf-wp-card" href="work-packages.qmd#wp4">
    <p class="pf-wp-number">WP4</p>
    <p class="pf-wp-title">Regulatory Framework &amp; Stakeholder Engagement</p>
    <p class="pf-wp-lead">Erasmus School of Law &amp; SCUT</p>
    <p class="pf-wp-desc">Regulatory analysis and participatory co-design to embed climate adaptation into governance frameworks.</p>
  </a>

</div>
```
